surfaces.part: bottom white and dark base strips

answer.evidence: The booth is a flat front view. Rows 0-3 are a front-facing white lintel strip with an outline and no sloped roof, edge line or eave shadow. The tan counter (rows 16-23) is a vertical face with a slot and wood-grain highlights; it has no separate receding top band. The monitor and the chair are decor. The white side posts and the base strips (rows 40-47) are also vertical faces. No horizontal top surface is visible for the roof, the counter or the base, so the whole object reads as a front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny booth, roughly one tile wide, with a monitor, desk and red chair inside a grey frame. It has no roof tiles, no wall plaster or stone and no door, so it does not read as a whole building like the references. The measured 17 visible tones per tile is above the references' 10-12, but that comes from a small, busy screen and desk cluster in a tiny footprint, not from material shading. Each material has only about 2-3 steps, where the references have 5-6 with per-tile highlights, scallops and speckle. The dark edge pixels are 100% near-neutral against 7-9% for the references, and the grey/black outline around every shape gives the sticker look rather than dark material-tone edges. Large surfaces such as the frame and the chair are flat, simple fills. It is far thinner and flatter than a Beodeul building.
